summary: TestUUIDPathOperationsDeclareBadRequest closes only the path-param subset — body/query/header 400 sources are still unguarded (TKT-110 follow-up)
description:
### Incidental finding spun out of TKT-110 (agent's own post-review verification, not the ai-review)

TKT-110 added `TestUUIDPathOperationsDeclareBadRequest`
(`services/catalog/internal/api/lifecycle_badrequest_test.go`), which closes a *class*: every catalog
operation with a `format: uuid` **path** parameter must declare `'400'`, because the oapi-codegen
binder can always reject one.

**That is one subset of the class, not the class.** The generated binder and the kin-openapi request
validator can also emit a 400 from:

- a **required `requestBody`** that is absent or schema-invalid (measured on TKT-110: invalid JSON,
  wrong property type, `minLength` violation, and a wrong `Content-Type` all produce 400 from the
  request validator),
- a **query parameter** that fails to bind or violates its schema,
- a **required header** parameter, same.

`getOpenAPISpec` is correctly outside this (it is served before validation).

**No current gap** — verified at TKT-110's merge: every catalog operation with a request body or a
constrained query/header parameter already declares `'400'`, and the nine that did not have one now do.
So this is latent, not live. But the invariant test's name and failure message speak only of path
parameters, and a future operation with a required body and no uuid path parameter would slip through
exactly the way these nine did — which is the failure mode ADR-028's corrected Consequences now
describe: *any status the binder or the request validator can write must be declared.*

**Scope to settle at plan time**

- [ ] Broaden the invariant to every rejection source the request layer has, or add a second invariant
      test per source — decide which reads better as a failure message
- [ ] Decide whether the same invariant belongs in the four non-codegen services. Their request
      validator does **not** reject malformed UUIDs today (`format: uuid` is unenforced repo-wide — no
      `EnableFormatValidation` / `DefineStringFormat` call exists), and their hand-rolled `parseUUID`
      400s *are* declared, so the answer may legitimately be no
- [ ] Related but separable: whether to enable `openapi3.EnableFormatValidation` at all. TKT-110
      explicitly rejected it as out of scope — it changes request-validation behaviour on every
      operation in all five services and could turn currently-succeeding requests into 400s. If that
      is ever adopted, this invariant's shape changes, so sequence them

**Governing:** ADR-028 (fail-closed on undeclared statuses, and its TKT-110 correction that the
carve-out does not hold for catalog), ADR-009 (spec is authoritative; any spec change ⇒ regen).

**Not urgent.** Nothing is broken today; this raises the ceiling on a test that currently prevents a
recurrence of nine real production defects.

governingAdrs.why: Its TKT-110-corrected Consequences state the rule this ticket would enforce more completely: for catalog, any status the binder or request validator can write must be declared, because response validation is the outermost wrap.
Spec-authoritative: if the outcome adds declarations, `make generate` runs and the regen is committed before the gate.

reference.summary: The test to broaden, and TKT-110's measurements of every 400 source it does not yet cover.
Source ticket with the full probe evidence (binder vs request validator, and why format:uuid is unenforced).

context.note: Minimal mémo baked at creation — born from a review-time finding, so it bypasses normal shaping (per decomposition.md).

All 8 items `met`. Ran the widened predicate over `services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml` at HEAD rather than inheriting TKT-110's merge-time verification:

**The one hard part is the proof, and it is called out in `success`.** A coverage ticket with no live defect cannot use red-then-green. The demonstration that works is a temporary spec mutation — remove a `'400'` from one body-bearing operation, show the **widened** test catches it and the **current** test does not, revert. Two runs. Without that comparison, "we widened the class" is exactly the unfalsifiable claim AGENTS.md warns about.

Three pieces of the existing test must survive the widening: the `Responses.Default()` arm (a `default:` response legitimately satisfies the invariant under kin-openapi), the deliberate absence of the hand-mounted `/internal/*` chi routes from the document, and the `getOpenAPISpec` exclusion. And widen the **failure message** too — it currently explains uuid path parameters, and a message that misstates why an operation owes a 400 aims the next reader at the wrong fix.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Plan draft — by `gpt-5.6-luna` (codex `task`, effort high)

Rung 1, one attempt, 7538 bytes, conclusive. The run showed the known local-skill hijack (it read `~/.ai/skills/unslop/SKILL.md`) — survivable per `codex-runner.md`, and it returned concrete, code-cited findings, so it is a pass. Verbatim below; my critique follows as `kind=plan-final`.

---

# DoD

- `services/catalog/internal/api/lifecycle_badrequest_test.go` checks every documented catalog operation with a request-layer 400 source.
- The test still accepts either an explicit `'400'` response or `default:`.
- `getOpenAPISpec` passes without a name-based exclusion.
- The test name and failure message no longer describe only UUID path parameters.
- The sibling runtime test remains valid and unchanged in behavior.
- Temporary mutations are reverted. `make check` passes with no generated-file or OpenAPI drift.
- Mutation evidence is recorded in the TKT-142 execution notes or PR description.

# Files touched

Final change:

- [services/catalog/internal/api/lifecycle_badrequest_test.go](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/api/lifecycle_badrequest_test.go:57)

Temporary proof mutation only, restored before completion:

- [services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml:51)
- [services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml:1049)

No production code, generated code, ADR, or OpenAPI change remains.

# Design

Rename `TestUUIDPathOperationsDeclareBadRequest` to:

```go
TestCatalogRequestRejectionSourcesDeclareBadRequest
```

Replace the UUID-only predicate with a predicate covering these sources:

```text
format: uuid path parameter
declared requestBody
query parameter
header parameter
```

The predicate should inspect both path-item and operation parameters, preserving the existing `item.Parameters` plus `op.Parameters` traversal. `$ref`s are already resolved by `openapi3.NewLoader().LoadFromData`, but each parameter reference should still be skipped when `ref.Value == nil`.

Use the following rules:

- A path parameter counts only when `in: path` and its schema format is `"uuid"`. Do not broaden this to every path parameter.
- Any non-nil, resolved `op.RequestBody` counts, regardless of `required`. A required body can be absent, and an optional body can still be schema-invalid when supplied.
- Any parameter with `in: query` or `in: header` counts. Missing required parameters, binding failures, and supplied values that violate the parameter schema can all produce 400.
- Keep the response check exactly as it is:

```go
op.Responses.Value("400") == nil && op.Responses.Default() == nil
```

The `Default()` arm is required because kin-openapi treats `default:` as matching 400.

The failure should describe the actual class, for example:

```text
operations with a catalog request-layer rejection source
(format:uuid path, request body, query, or header) can return 400;
ADR-028 turns an undeclared 400 into 500, so each must declare
'400' or 'default'. Missing on ...
```

Update the surrounding comments in the file so they explain the broader invariant. Keep the existing runtime test, `TestLifecycleRejectionsAreDeclaredBadRequests`, unchanged in its request coverage. It already proves the real 400 behavior for malformed UUID binding and an invalid request body. The widened test is a spec-level class check, not a replacement for those runtime assertions.

The two documented internal operations are in scope because they are generated routes present in `doc.Paths.Map()`:

- `resolvePerformanceDisplayNames` has required query parameters at [openapi.yaml:1037](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml:1037).
- `resolveTicketTypeFees` has a UUID path parameter and query parameter at [openapi.yaml:1103](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml:1103).

The other hand-mounted `/internal/*` routes are absent from the OpenAPI document and therefore correctly outside this spec traversal. `getOpenAPISpec` is also excluded structurally because it has no parameters or request body. Do not add a name-based exception.

# Test plan / proof of the gap

Use two temporary mutations because body and query are distinct newly-covered source branches. Both selected operations have no UUID path parameter, so the old test cannot catch either mutation.

Run each mutation separately, with no gate or generator running.

| Mutation | Why it proves the gap |
|---|---|
| Remove the `'400'` response from `POST /venues`, operation `createVenue`, at [openapi.yaml:51](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml:51) | Required request body, no path parameters |
| Remove the `'400'` response from `GET /internal/performances/display-names`, operation `resolvePerformanceDisplayNames`, at [openapi.yaml:1049](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml:1049) | Required query parameters, no UUID path parameter |

For each mutation:

1. Run the current test before changing the test implementation:

   ```sh
   cd services/catalog
   go test -count=1 ./internal/api \
     -run '^TestUUIDPathOperationsDeclareBadRequest$'
   ```

   Expected result: pass. The old predicate does not inspect the selected body or query source.

2. Apply the widened test implementation and run:

   ```sh
   go test -count=1 ./internal/api \
     -run '^TestCatalogRequestRejectionSourcesDeclareBadRequest$'
   ```

   Expected result: fail and identify the mutated operation, such as:

   ```text
   Missing on 1:
     post /venues (createVenue)
   ```

3. Restore the exact `'400'` line before starting the next mutation.

4. Record both results, including the command, mutation, and expected pass/fail, in the TKT-142 execution notes or PR description.

The temporary change only affects the embedded `services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml` read by `services/catalog/api/spec.go`. Do not run `make generate` while the temporary response is removed, and do not leave any generated output from the experiment. Verify that the temporary OpenAPI diff is empty before the final gate.

After restoring the spec:

```sh
cd services/catalog
go test -count=1 ./internal/api \
  -run '^TestCatalogRequestRejectionSourcesDeclareBadRequest$'
go test -count=1 ./internal/api \
  -run '^TestLifecycleRejectionsAreDeclaredBadRequests$'
cd ../..
make check
```

# Risks

- Counting only `required: true` request bodies would miss malformed optional bodies such as `closeSlot`. Count every resolved request body.
- Counting only operation-level parameters would miss path-item parameters. Preserve both parameter sets.
- Counting every path parameter would expand the invariant beyond the stated UUID binder guarantee and may create false positives.
- A future optional query or header parameter still belongs in the predicate because an invalid supplied value can be rejected with 400.
- The current specification has no header parameters, so the header branch has no live mutation proof. The implementation must still include it for future operations.
- Removing a response from the temporary spec while running `make generate` or `make check` could create misleading generated drift. Keep the mutation isolated, restore it, then run the gate.
- The invariant checks declaration coverage, not every runtime rejection path. That is appropriate here because the existing sibling test already exercises representative runtime behavior.

# Open decisions

None. The settled scope supports one final test-file change, with body and query mutations used to prove that the widened predicate catches gaps invisible to the current UUID-only predicate.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan-final -->
### Plan critique + final — critique by `main-agent` (planReview), gate 2 taken autonomously

Cross-model pair holds: drafted by `gpt-5.6-luna`, critiqued by `main-agent`. **The `kind=plan` draft as amended below is the plan.**

#### Seam verification (every symbol and line the draft names, checked at HEAD)

| Draft's claim | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `TestUUIDPathOperationsDeclareBadRequest` at `lifecycle_badrequest_test.go` | ✅ exists |
| `createVenue` `'400'` at `openapi.yaml:51` | ✅ exact — `'400': $ref '#/components/responses/BadRequest'` |
| `resolvePerformanceDisplayNames` `'400'` at `openapi.yaml:1049` | ✅ exact |
| `resolveTicketTypeFees` has uuid path + query | ✅ |
| kin-openapi resolves `$ref` parameters | ✅ **executed**, not assumed — 42 ops, `nilParamRefs=0`, 21 request bodies, **0 header parameters** |
| `closeSlot` body is `required: false` | ✅ line 487 — the draft's "count every resolved body, not just required" risk is real and correctly reasoned |
| `EnableFormatValidation` / `DefineStringFormat` absent repo-wide | ✅ zero hits |

#### Accepted from the draft

The predicate shape (uuid path OR any resolved requestBody OR any query OR any header), both parameter sets traversed, the `Responses.Default()` arm kept verbatim, the rename, the widened failure message, the structural (not name-based) exclusion of `getOpenAPISpec`, two mutations rather than one, and the "no `make generate` while mutated" caution. All of it survives review.

#### Amendment 1 — the predicate is now extensionally near-total, and the plan must say so

I ran the widened predicate at HEAD. It selects **41 of 42** operations; the sole exclusion is `getOpenAPISpec`. So today the predicate is *equivalent to* "every operation except the spec-serving one".

The draft does not state this, and it matters in two directions:

- **It vindicates the structural exclusion.** `getOpenAPISpec` drops out because it has no parameters and no body, not because of its name. That is the right construction and it should be commented as such, so a future reader does not "simplify" the predicate into a name check.
- **It is also the honest limit of the test.** A predicate that admits almost everything discriminates almost nothing *today*. Its value is entirely prospective: it fires on the future operation that has a body and no uuid path parameter. The comment must say that, or the next reader over-reads the test's strength.

This is a documentation amendment, not a design change — the design is right.

#### Amendment 2 — the header branch is unprovable today; label it, do not fake it

Zero header parameters exist in the spec (executed). The draft flags this in Risks but then leaves the branch unproven. Per AGENTS.md, a branch a fixture cannot reach is exactly the thing that looks like coverage and is not. **Do not** invent a header parameter in the spec to manufacture a proof — that mutates the contract to suit a test.

Resolution: keep the header branch (it is correct and costs one line), and state in the stage comment and the test comment that it is **unexercised by construction — no header parameter exists in this document**. An honest "this branch has no live proof" beats a fabricated one.

#### Amendment 3 — the mutation must run in BOTH directions, per-mutation

The draft says: old test passes, new test fails. That is the right comparison, but the run order in step 1/2 replaces the test implementation between the two runs, which risks conflating "the predicate widened" with "I edited the file". Tighten to: with **each** mutation applied, run **both** test functions from the **same** working tree (the widened file keeps the old function too during the demonstration, or the two are compared across a stash) — old green, new red, same tree, same command. Then revert the spec and confirm both green. Four observations per mutation, not two.

#### Amendment 4 — assert the spec is pristine before the gate

The draft says "verify the temporary OpenAPI diff is empty". Make it mechanical: `git diff --exit-code services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml` before running `make check`. ADR-009's regen rule makes a stray spec byte expensive (`check-generate` diffs against HEAD).

#### Rejected

Nothing. The draft had no defects of design — only two things left unsaid (Amendments 1–2) and two things left informal (3–4).

#### Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model

Amendments 1, 2, 3 and 4 above. All four are **additive constraints on evidence and comments**; none changes the predicate, the file set, or the test's logic, so the code that ships is still the cross-reviewed draft's design. Flagging them again here and at review hand-off per the skill's rule.

#### Decisions taken autonomously at Gate 2 (`config.gates: autonomous`)

The draft recorded **"Open decisions: none"**, and my critique opened none, so there was no contested option to resolve. The one judgement call I did make — Amendment 2, keep the unprovable header branch and label it, rather than dropping it or fabricating a spec header — follows the **most reversible** option per the autonomous rule: a labelled unexercised branch is deleted in one line later, whereas a contract mutated to suit a test is a spec change that outlives the ticket.

**`risk:low` remains NOT claimed** (see `kind=claim`). Blast radius is one test file, but the ticket's central question was the falsifiability of the proof — and the plan gate earned itself here: Amendments 1 and 3 are both about the proof's honesty.

→ transition `Planning` → `Building`, label `agent:coding`.

### Implementation — by `main-agent` (`config.models.implement`), PR [#319](https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/319)

```yaml

commit: 0d2ee7f9
pr: 319
files: 2
gate: make check — sentinel EXIT=0, log body grepped clean (1319 lines, zero Error/FAIL/drifted/panic)
```

**Delivered:** predicate widened to all four rejection sources; `TestUUIDPathOperationsDeclareBadRequest` → `TestCatalogRequestRejectionSourcesDeclareBadRequest`; `hasUUIDPathParam` → `hasRejectionSource(pathParams, opParams, body)`; failure message rewritten; ADR-028's stale symbol reference updated.

#### Proof of the gap — the deliverable's actual evidence

Per Amendment 3, both tests ran from **one working tree** with each mutation applied — four observations per mutation, not two.

| Mutation | old test | widened test |
|---|---|---|
| `'400'` off `createVenue` (required body, no path param) | **PASS** | **FAIL** — `POST /venues (createVenue)` |
| `'400'` off `resolvePerformanceDisplayNames` (required query, no uuid path param) | **PASS** | **FAIL** — that exact operation |
| both reverted | PASS | **PASS** |

Both targets are invisible to the *old* predicate by construction — had they not been, the comparison would have proved nothing.

**Plus a predicate mutation** (the AGENTS.md "is the mechanism inert?" check, in its meaningful form): disabling the body arm *while the `createVenue` gap is present* leaves the test **green**. That is the reading that matters — the arm is live and load-bearing, not decoration. A bare predicate mutant with a pristine spec stays green for an uninteresting reason and proves nothing, so it was not used as the check.

#### Amendment compliance (all four from `kind=plan-final`)

1. ✅ The 41-of-42 extensional limit is stated in the test comment — prospective value, not present discrimination.
2. ✅ Header arm kept and **labelled unexercised by construction**. Not faked: no header parameter was invented in the spec.
3. ✅ One-working-tree, both-directions comparison, per mutation (table above).
4. ✅ `git diff --exit-code services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml` asserted pristine before the gate. No `make generate` ran while mutated; no regen artifacts.

#### Deviation from the plan — one, additive

The plan scoped the change to **one file**. I touched a second: `docs/adr/ADR-028-response-drift-fail-closed.md` named `TestUUIDPathOperationsDeclareBadRequest` **by symbol** while its surrounding sentence describes the broader rule the test did not yet enforce. Renaming the symbol without it would leave the ADR pointing at nothing. Neither the drafter nor I caught it at plan time — a `grep` for the old symbol after the rename did. In scope as a consequence of the rename, and it makes the ADR true for the first time.

→ label `agent:coding` → `agent:ai-review`.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ai-review kind=summary -->
### Adversarial review — by `gpt-5.6-luna` (codex `adversarial-review`), **four passes, stopped at the absolute cap**

Cross-model pair holds: implemented by `main-agent`, reviewed by `gpt-5.6-luna`. All four runs were conclusive and non-empty (bytes asserted before reading, per `codex-runner.md`).

| Pass | Base | Findings | Non-trivial fixes? → next pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `origin/main` | 2 (1 high, 1 medium) | yes — both correctness |
| 2 | `0d2ee7f9` | 2 (medium ×2) | yes — structural refactor |
| 3 | `6f3e901b` | 3 (medium ×3) | yes — two new arms |
| 4 | `ac5123d1` | 2 (1 medium, 1 low) | **cap reached** |

#### ⚠ Stopped at the cap with an unreviewed fix diff

Pass 4's fixes (commit `22f75610` — the content-backed arm, and typed-error matching) are **the branch's least-reviewed commit**. Findings went 2 → 2 → 3 → 2, which is **not strictly decreasing**, so the convergence exception to the 4-pass cap does not apply and the cap holds. The residual risk is **unquantified**, and my own verification of that last commit is **my own work, not a second model's** — recorded here and in the review-guide as the rule requires.

#### Per-finding verdicts

**Pass 1**
- `[high]` *optional parameters create false 400 obligations* — **partially accepted, fixed differently.** The premise (optional ⇒ unrejectable) is **false**, and the spec disproves it: `channel_code` is `required: false` with `minLength: 1`, and `?channel_code=` answers `400 "minimum string length is 1"` — executed, not argued. The reviewer's proposed fix (count only `required`) would have introduced a false negative. The real line is **constrained-vs-schemaless**, and that is what shipped.
- `[medium]` *`4XX` ranges rejected* — **accepted, real.** `ValidateResponse` resolves via `Responses.Status(400)`, which matches the exact key **and** the `4XX` range; the test read `Value("400")`. I had found this independently while the pass ran. Fixed by using the same matcher the validated code uses.

**Pass 2**
- `[medium]` *helper duplicates the invariant logic* — **accepted, real, and the most valuable finding of the run.** The synthetic cases had their own copy of the scan, so they pinned the harness rather than the contract. Extracted `operationsMissingBadRequest`; both tiers now run it.
- `[medium]` *schemaless fixture is not a valid OpenAPI document* — **accepted, real.** `doc.Validate` rejects it, and catalog's `NewRouter` validates before serving, so the fixture could never reach a router. Valid cases now assert `doc.Validate` passes; the invalid one is quarantined in its own test that says what it actually covers.

**Pass 3**
- `[medium]` *quarantine doesn't prove WHY validation failed* — **accepted** (I had already tightened this while the pass ran).
- `[medium]` *`default:` arm untested* — **accepted, real.** The failure message promises the spelling; nothing exercised it.
- `[medium]` *header arm untested* — **accepted, real, and it corrected a false claim of mine.** I had written "unexercised by construction". True of the live spec; **false as a claim about the test** — a synthetic document reaches it fine. The comment is fixed along with the gap.

**Pass 4**
- `[medium]` *content-backed arm uncovered* — **accepted, real.** `p.Schema != nil || p.Content != nil` short-circuits and every fixture declared `schema:`, so the second operand never evaluated.
- `[low]` *error-string matching despite typed errors* — **accepted, and it refuted a claim I wrote one commit earlier.** I had commented that kin-openapi exposes no typed error; it exports `*openapi3.ParameterContentSchemaExactlyOne`. Now matched with `errors.As`.

Pass 4 also **refuted two of its own attack lines** by checking them: the default-only fixture does validate, and the header subtest is discriminating. Both agree with my independent checks.

#### Mutation ledger — every fix, one mutant, observed red

Fix-time tests get the same discipline as planned ones. Each mutant was run **individually** and reddens **only** its own case:

| Mutant | Result |
|---|---|
| `Status(400)` → `Value("400")` | only *4XX range* reddens |
| schemaless guard removed | only *schemaless* reddens |
| **shared** scanner's predicate broken | edge cases redden — **proves the refactor**; under the duplicated version they stayed green |
| `Default()` fallback removed | only *default response alone* reddens |
| parameter switch narrowed to query-only | only *header* reddens |
| `p.Content != nil` removed | only *content-backed* reddens |
| quarantine fixture invalid for an unrelated reason (`in: bogus`) | only quarantined test reddens |

And the ticket's own deliverable — the gap demonstration — was **re-run against the final predicate**, not just the first: with `createVenue`'s `'400'` removed, the test fails naming `POST /venues (createVenue)`, identical output to before the refactor (behaviour-preservation, checked by running it, which also refuted pass 3's attack line 1).

#### Final state

`+279/−25`, 2 files, 5 commits. Live invariant + 6 synthetic edge cases + 1 quarantined loader test. Every branch of `hasRejectionSource` and `operationsMissingBadRequest` now has a covering test that fails when that branch is removed — **except** the non-uuid path arm and the nil-ref guard, which are refusal/defensive paths (pass 4 named them; neither can produce a false negative).

`make check` green: sentinel `EXIT=0`, log body grepped clean, 1319 lines.

→ label `agent:ai-review` → `needs:human`; review-guide posted on the PR. **Stopping pushes.**

| **No live gap introduced** | 42 operations, 41 carry a rejection source, all declare a 400; `getOpenAPISpec` is the sole exclusion and has no rejection source |
| **`make check` green** | on the branch (`EXIT=0`, 1319 lines clean) and in CI (`check` pass 8m39s, `gate-selftest` pass) |
| **The gap is demonstrated** — the item shaping flagged as needing the most care | two-way spec mutation, re-run against the *final* predicate: old test PASS / widened test FAIL naming the operation, for a body source and a query source; both reverted, spec byte-identical |

#### The three things shaping said must survive the widening

1. **`Responses.Default()` arm** — survives, and is now the only arm with its own test (`default response alone satisfies the invariant`); it was untested before this ticket.
2. **Hand-mounted `/internal/*` chi routes stay out of reach** — unchanged: they are absent from the document and mounted outside the validator. The two `/internal/*` paths that *are* documented are in scope like any other operation, as before.
3. **`getOpenAPISpec` excluded** — survives, and is now excluded *structurally* (no parameters, no body ⇒ no rejection source) rather than by name.

Plus the fourth thing shaping asked for: the **failure message was widened**, so it no longer explains uuid-path reasoning for an operation that owes a 400 for some other reason.

#### What the owner should know before accepting

- **The last commit (`22f75610`) was not reviewed by a second model** — four adversarial passes ran, the absolute cap is four, and findings (2→2→3→2) were not strictly decreasing, so the convergence exception did not apply. Residual risk **unquantified**; my verification of that commit is my own. It is small: one test case plus a typed-error swap, both mutation-checked. Carried in `overrides:` below.
- **The invariant discriminates little today** (41 of 42 operations). Its value is prospective — it fires on the future operation with a body/query/header and no uuid path parameter, which is exactly how TKT-110's nine defects arose. Stated in the test comment so it is not over-read.
- **ADR-028 was edited**, because its Consequences named the renamed test by symbol while describing the broader rule the test did not yet enforce. It now describes what the code actually does.

→ transitioning `PO Review` → `Done`.

<!-- sdlc:stage=done kind=metrics -->
### Closeout — TKT-142

Merged `f75d73f4` (PR #319, squash, branch deleted). Post-merge gate on `main`: `EXIT=0`, 1332 lines clean.

#### Durations (from the `sdlc-state` commit log)

| stage | duration |
|---|---|
| Backlog (created → Ready) | ~5h 25m (2026-07-29 creation → prioritized) |
| Ready → Planning (claim) | 7h 01m — queue time, not work |
| `agent:planning` (draft by `gpt-5.6-luna`) | 5m 23s |
| `agent:plan-review` (critique by `main-agent`) | 1m 13s |
| Planning → Building | 08:58:57 |
| `agent:coding` (TDD + gap demonstration + first gate) | 11m 22s |
| `agent:ai-review` (4 passes + 4 fix rounds + 4 gates) | 1h 16m 22s |
| Building → PO Review | 10:26:42 |
| PO Review → Done | self-validated, same session |
| **total in-flight (Ready → Done)** | **~1h 34m** |

`human-wait total`: **n/a (autonomous)** — no gate waited on a human.
`diff`: **+279 / −25 (2 files)**, 5 commits squashed to 1.

#### overrides:

Gates 2, 3 and 4 were taken by agent judgement. One item to re-take:

1. **Stopped at the 4-pass cap with an unreviewed fix diff.**
   - *Finding / situation:* pass 4 returned 2 findings (`[medium]` uncovered `content:` arm, `[low]` error-string matching). Both were fixed in `22f75610`. That commit was then **not** reviewed by a second model.
   - *Reviewer's position:* pass 4's verdict was `needs-attention` — i.e. "do not ship yet" — and it had been `needs-attention` on all four passes.
   - *Agent's reason:* the absolute cap is 4 passes, and the convergence exception requires findings **strictly decreasing**; they went 2 → 2 → 3 → 2. The exception did not apply, so the rule says stop and hand over. I stopped, fixed the two findings (both mutation-checked), and recorded the residual rather than running a fifth pass.
   - *Residual risk carried by:* **this ticket, unquantified.** The unreviewed change is one test case for the `content:` arm plus an `errors.As` swap. No production code. If the owner wants it closed, a single review pass on `22f75610` is the whole ask.

Everything else the reviewer raised was accepted and fixed; nothing blocking was overridden on the merits. `risk:low` was **not** claimed (justified in `kind=claim`), so no gate was skipped on that basis.

#### learnings:

1. **A predicate built from `A || B` is one test away from a lie — `||` short-circuits past the second operand.** Every fixture declared `schema:`, so `p.Content != nil` was never evaluated and deleting it kept the suite green. This is the AGENTS.md "green test that cannot reach the failing state" rule specialized to boolean operators, and it is *invisible* to single-mutation testing of the arm you happened to think of. **Target house:** repo-local — `docs/learnings/`, cross-referenced from AGENTS.md's existing green-test cluster. Worth writing up because the general rule is already in AGENTS.md and this is the operator-level tell that makes it actionable: *for an N-way disjunction, you owe N fixtures, each satisfying exactly one operand.*

2. **"Unexercised by construction" is a claim about the LIVE fixture, not about the test — and the two get conflated.** I wrote that the header arm could not be tested because the catalog document declares no header parameter. True of the document; false of the test, which builds synthetic documents and reaches the arm trivially. The honest-sounding label ("this branch has no live proof") is *more* dangerous than silence, because it reads as diligence and closes the question. **Target house:** repo-local, same learning file as (1). The rule: before labelling a branch untestable, ask *untestable by what fixture?* — if you control the fixture, you do not have that excuse.

3. **A test asserting "this fixture is invalid" must assert WHY, by typed error where one exists.** Both a bare `err != nil` and a message-substring match survive the fixture breaking for an unrelated reason. Caught by review twice in a row here — first the bare check, then my own comment falsely claiming no typed error existed. **Target house:** repo-local.

4. **Process, for the skill:** the `codex-runner.md` rule "a codex invocation is the ONLY command in its Bash call" has a **cwd twin**. My shell was left in `services/catalog` by an earlier call, and `make check` exited 2 on `No rule to make target 'check'` — TKT-71's exact shape, which AGENTS.md already names. The harness reported that background job as "exit code 0" while the sentinel said `EXIT=2`: **the sentinel was right and the harness was wrong**, which is precisely why the sentinel rule exists. No skill edit needed — both rules are already written and both worked. Recording it as **evidence the existing rule earns its place**, not as a new one.

#### retro:

**(1) What would have made this ticket faster or better?**

The plan gate did its job and the shaping was excellent — `readiness.success` predicted the hard part exactly ("a coverage ticket cannot use red-then-green; the demonstration is a temporary spec mutation") and that is what shipped. What cost the time was **four review passes on a two-file test-only change**, each finding a real defect in the previous fix. That is not waste — every pass caught something a human reviewer would likely have missed — but it is worth naming the pattern: *the ticket's subject was "make this test honest", and each pass simply applied that same standard one level deeper.* A plan that had said "enumerate every branch of the predicate and name its covering fixture **before** writing the first test" would plausibly have collapsed passes 3 and 4 into pass 1. **Concrete, appliable:** add to `references/quality-practices.md` §1 (pre-mortem) a line for test-authoring tickets — *"if the deliverable is a predicate, the plan must enumerate its branches and the fixture covering each; a branch with no named fixture is a finding at plan time, not at review time."*

**(2) What should the humans change?**

Nothing in the process — it worked as designed, and the cap held correctly under pressure to keep going. One observation for the owner: `config.models.aiReview` = `gpt-5.6-luna` performed **very** well on this ticket (8 real findings across 4 passes, two of which refuted false claims in my own comments, and it refuted two of its own attack lines by checking them). Contrast with `~/.claude/ab-tests/results.jsonl`, where the `luna:xhigh@claudex` arm is recorded as emitting tool-call stubs. The bare `gpt-5.6-luna` via codex `adversarial-review` is a good default and this run is a data point worth keeping.

**Offer:** I can apply retro item (1) to `references/quality-practices.md` now — say the word. Items (1)–(3) under `learnings:` want a single `docs/learnings/` entry; that is a documentation change and per the skill's own rules goes **direct to `main`**, no ticket. I have not written it without your go-ahead.

objective.note: TestUUIDPathOperationsDeclareBadRequest closes a CLASS by design — that is its stated point and why it is spec-only. But the class it actually closes is narrower than the class that exists: the binder and the kin-openapi request validator also emit 400 from a required requestBody, a constrained query parameter and a required header. A future operation with a body and no uuid path parameter slips through exactly the way the nine that TKT-110 fixed did, and under ADR-028 an undeclared 400 becomes a 500.

scope.note: IN: services/catalog/internal/api/lifecycle_badrequest_test.go — widen the predicate from 'has a format:uuid path parameter' to the full set of binder/validator 400 sources, and correct the test name and failure message, which today speak only of path parameters. OUT: fixing catalog operations (there are none to fix — see uncertainties). OUT: the other four services, which have their own specs and their own version of this test or none; TKT-256 is already handling payments' sibling shape for 500.

uncertainties.note: The load-bearing one — 'is this still latent, or has a live gap appeared since TKT-110 merged?' — was settled by running the widened predicate over the spec at HEAD rather than trusting the ticket's 'verified at TKT-110's merge'. Result: **zero** live gaps. Every catalog operation with a requestBody or a constrained query/header parameter already declares '400'. So this ticket is pure invariant-widening with no accompanying spec fix, which is the clean case. Second, smaller: `getOpenAPISpec` is correctly outside the class (served before validation) and the hand-mounted /internal/* chi routes are absent from the document entirely — both already handled by the existing test's structure, both must survive the widening.

dependencies.note: None. No blockers. TKT-110 (the origin) is Done.

approach.note: Verified against the test at HEAD before inheriting the ticket's framing. The existing test is already the right shape — spec-only, drives no requests, covers operation number ten without a fixture — so this is a predicate widening inside a good structure, not a rewrite. Three details the drafter must preserve: (1) the `op.Responses.Default() == nil` arm, which is there because a `default:` response satisfies 400 under kin-openapi's status matching and without it a contract-correct future operation fails; (2) the deliberate absence of the /internal/* chi routes from the document; (3) the exclusion of `getOpenAPISpec`. The failure message must be widened too — it currently explains the uuid-path-parameter reasoning, and a message that misstates WHY an operation owes a 400 sends the next reader to the wrong fix.

first_slice.note: The whole ticket is one slice — one predicate, one name, one message. The four 400 sources could be added one at a time but there is no reason to: they share the predicate's structure and the spec has no live gap for any of them.

success.note: **This is the item that needs the most care, because the ticket is a coverage ticket with no live defect — so the ordinary proof (the test goes red, then the fix makes it green) is unavailable.** AGENTS.md's rule still applies: demonstrate the gap. The honest demonstration here is a temporary spec mutation — add or take a body/query-parameter 400 off one operation, show the widened test catches it and the CURRENT test does not, then revert. That two-run comparison IS the deliverable's evidence; without it 'we widened the invariant' is unfalsifiable, and per AGENTS.md a green test that cannot reach the failing state looks exactly like one that proves something. Then: the test name and message speak of the real class, no live gap is introduced, `make check` green.

context_memo.note: governingAdrs (resolve at HEAD): ADR-028 (docs/adr/ADR-028-response-drift-fail-closed.md) — the fail-closed validation that turns an undeclared 400 into a 500, i.e. the entire reason this invariant is worth having; ADR-009 (docs/adr/ADR-009-contract-first-apis.md) — contract-first and the regen-before-gate rule, relevant only if a spec line is touched. governingTests: services/catalog/internal/api/lifecycle_badrequest_test.go — the subject itself, whose `hasUUIDPathParam` helper and `default:` arm carry the reasoning above. Sibling worth reading, not editing: TKT-256 is widening the same invariant shape for 500 in payments; if both land, the two tests should be recognisable as the same pattern.
